description: Deterministic passive interpolation using a time-varying linear gain estimated from training sweeps. For each time sample t, we fit a zero-intercept ordinary least-squares slope g(t) between voltage deflection and injected current across the four training amplitudes: g(t) = sum_j x_j(t)*y_j(t) / sum_j x_j(t)^2. This yields the step response shape per unit current. We then smooth g(t) with a short symmetric Hamming window, calibrate its steady-state scale to match the slope estimated from the last 20% of samples (preserving the correct resistance), and enforce physical constraints (non-negativity, monotonic increase via cumulative maximum, and g(0)=0). Predictions for the two held-out sweeps are obtained by pointwise multiplication y_pred(t) = g_hat(t) * x_test(t). No test labels are used; rows are treated independently; only linear passive interpolation within a single cell is assumed. The method is vectorized, uses no randomness, and returns finite outputs with the same shape as test_x.
